title: What If You Dropped a Hammer and a Feather on the Moon?

scenes.text: What if you dropped a hammer and a feather on the Moon? An astronaut actually did.
On Earth the hammer wins easily. The feather drifts, because air pushes back on it.
In 1971, Apollo 15 commander David Scott held both out from about 1.6 meters up.
The hammer weighed about 1.3 kilograms. The feather was a falcon feather, hundreds of times lighter.
He let go of both at the same moment, with the cameras rolling.
They hit the lunar dust together. With no air, gravity pulls everything at the same rate. Galileo was right.

description:
What if you dropped a hammer and a feather on the Moon?
